LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.

MATERIALS
•	 P&P SB4 Page 4 Stickers
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
This worksheet shows different countries and an arrow 
pointing to a question mark. The Ss must use the past tense 
to say what can be seen or visited in each country and place 
the correct sticker on top of the question mark. 
First review the countries by asking, “What country is this?” 
and then the stickers by asking, “What is this?” to which students 
must reply for example, “It’s the Alhambra.” 
Ss have to take turns asking their classmates what they saw 
or visited in each country. Model the activity for the students

before starting. Ask a confident S, “Which country did you 
go to?”. That S should answer, “I went to Spain.”. Next, ask 
them “What did you visit there?”, to which they should reply, 
“I visited the Alhambra.”. Have all the Ss put the Alhambra 
sticker on the question mark next to Spain.
Ss should take turns to ask and answer questions following 
the model.
> Follow-Up
Say one incorrect phrase to each S and have them correct 
you. Say, for example, “I went to India and I visited the Big 
Ben.” and the S should reply, “No, that’s wrong! You went to 
India and you visited the Taj Tahal.”
> Advanced Groups
This is the same activity as in Day 1, but with different 
countries. Your group might be familiar with the structures and 
the vocabulary, so you can have the Ss work in pairs asking 
and answering the questions above. You could also have them 
ask and reply in two big groups.
For the follow-up, you could have them come up with incorrect 
statements themselves.

TARGET LANGUAGE
I saw elephants in South Africa.
I saw kangaroos in Australia.
I saw polar bears in Canada.
I saw lemurs in Madagascar.
I visited the Statue of Liberty in the United States of 
America.
I visited the pyramids in Egypt.
I visited the Great Wall in China.
I visited the Taj Mahal in India.
I visited Big Ben in England.
I visited the Alhambra in Spain.
I visited the Eiffel Tower in France.
I went to the Black Forest in Germany.
I visited the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy.
I visited Christ the Redeemer in Brazil.
I visited Mount Fuji in Japan.
I visited Patagonia in Argentina.
> Warm-Up
Take a country from the bag and describe your imaginary 
trip. For example, show the South Africa cutout and say, “Last 
year, I went to South Africa, and I saw the elephants there!” 
Then stick that country on the map. Repeat with three more 
countries.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Use Blu-Tack to stick the Map (P.4.1) up on the whiteboard. 
Then take the Country cutouts and put them in a cloth bag.

The Ss take it in turns to take a country from the bag. Ask the 
S, “Where did you go?” and have them respond by saying, “I 
went to Brazil.” Then ask, “What did you visit in Brazil?”, 
and have the S respond according to what is pictured on the 
cutout, “I visited Christ the Redeemer in Brazil.”. Then the S 
places the country on the map in the correct space. Do as many 
countries as time allows.
NOTE: your Ss are likely to need support the first couple 
times you do this activity. Do not hesitate to help them come 
up with the name of the places. Accept any other ideas as long 
as they are correct, and the S has used the target structure. 
> Advanced Groups
You can let your Ss ask the target questions (“Where did you 
go?” and “What did you visit in…?”) to the S who has taken 
a country cutout.
6.– ACTIVITY 6: TRAVEL TIPS (7’)
P.4.2
England
P.4.7
> How to Play
Ss should find matching pairs of countries (P.4.2) and the 
things that they can see or visit there (P.4.7). When they get a 
correct match, Ss must give advice on what to do there. 
> Warm-Up
Take a country card (P.4.2) at random and say “I’m going to 
Japan. What should I visit?” to which Ss should reply, “If you 
go to Japan, you should visit Mount Fuji.” Try to quickly review 
at least five more countries.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Before class, prepare decks consisting of six cards: three 
countries, and three things you can do there (one per country). 
You will need as many decks as pairs of Ss in your group.

Put the Ss into pairs. Deal S1 the country cards and S2 the 
activity cards. S1 takes a country card and says for example, 
“I’m going to Italy. What should I visit?”. Then S2 looks for the 
corresponding card in their deck, shows it to their partner and 
says, “If you go to Italy, you should visit the Leaning Tower 
of Pisa.” Give each S at least two pairs to work on. 
If time allows, redistribute the different decks and change 
their roles (from asking for advice to giving it, and vice versa). 
> Follow-Up
Take two cards that don’t match and say for example, “If 
you go to Canada, you should visit the Eiffel Tower.”. Ss will 
see that it is not correct so encourage them to correct you by 
saying, “No, that’s wrong. If you go to Canada, you should 
see polar bears.”
NOTE: accept other options that the Ss might come up with, 
if they are correct and they use the proper structure.
7.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and 
do the challenge.

•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.

> Main Activity
The goal of the game is to find as many cards as possible. 
Stick some of the Number Cards (P.E.M.3.) on the wall (out 
of reach of the Ss, so they can’t damage them). Say, “Find 
number...” and have the Ss run and point to the corresponding 
number. When the S points to the correct number, take it off 
the wall and keep it as a point for that S. The S who collects 
the most cards wins. 
NOTE: this game can become hectic if everybody is playing 
at the same time. It is advisable to play this game in duels of 
two Ss (S1 vs S2). You call out the number and the two Ss must 
race to point to the card first.
